Why split. The supplied proof has two independent obligations.
- Steps 1–3 show that Λ(ω) = c∫ω(e) dLⁿ is linear and sequentially continuous for the test-form topology. This is the special case R = (ℝⁿ, |c|, sign(c)·ε) of the general reusable fact "an integer multiplicity triple defines a current" (Simon 6.3.1 (‡)). The same type is also accepted as rsd_cmr_imrep_represents_exists.
- Steps 4–6 build an explicit IMRep whose action is c∫ω(e). This is the new child unit_imrep (dtc_bc_cz_unit_current_imrep).

Reusing the first part removes the analytic sequential-continuity estimate from new formal work. The leaf cannot otherwise use dtc_imrep_current: this node's proof base 72492511a does not contain 642d7450f (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 1). 3. IsIntegerMultiplicity C holds with witness R, and C(ω) = R.action ω = c·∫ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y). ∎

This is the supplied proof, reorganized:
- C takes the same values as the functional Λ of steps 2–3 (both equal c∫ω(e) at every ω).

subproblems.title: The integer multiplicity triple of c[[ℝⁿ]] and its action
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and c ∈ ℤ. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in U = ℝⁿ, i.e. R ∈ IMRep univ n: M ⊆ ℝⁿ is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ : ℝⁿ → ℕ is measurable, positive on M and locally Hⁿ-integrable, and ξ : ℝⁿ → Λₙ(ℝⁿ) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, a unit orientation ±τ₁∧…∧τₙ (τ orthonormal) of an approximate tangent space of M. Its action satisfies R.action ω = ∫_M θ(y)⟨ω(y), ξ(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y) = c·∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ) (TestFormOn univ n), where e = (e₁, …, eₙ) is the standard basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Only existence is asserted; the proof takes R = (∅, 0, 0) if c = 0 and R = (ℝⁿ, |c|, sign(c)·e₁∧…∧eₙ) if c ≠ 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (c : ℤ), 0 < n → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid n)) n, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) = (c : ℝ) * ∫ y, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid n) n) y ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the supplied proof of dtc_bc_cz_unit_current (the integer multiplicity representation of C = c[[ℝⁿ]] and the computation of its action), stated here for the triple itself. Book references (local copy book/chapter-06.txt): Simon 6.2.2 (line 203, [[M]](ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x)), 6.2.34 (line 572, [[U]] with the standard orientation e₁∧…∧eₙ) and 6.3.1 (‡) (lines 733–753, T(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ θ(x) dHⁿ(x)). No sibling is used, and the hypothesis 0 < n is not needed.
Notation: e := ⇑(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ), the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ = Euclid n, so ‖e_i‖ = 1. Hⁿ := μHE[n] and Lⁿ := volume. On Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) we have Hⁿ = Lⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n). Let ε : MultiVector n n = (Covector (Euclid n) n →L[ℝ] ℝ) be the evaluation ε(α) := α(e). It is linear in α and continuous: it is ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid n) ℝ e. Equivalently it is LinearMap.mkContinuous with bound 1, since |α(e)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ‖eᵢ‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
1. Case c = 0. Let R₀ have carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0. Its IMRep fields hold:
(a) ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ univ.
(b) CountablyRectifiable n ∅ holds by Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, because Hⁿ(∅) = 0.
(c) The constant function 0 is measurable. mult_pos is vacuous, since no point lies in ∅.
(d) For every compact K, ∫⁻_{∅∩K} 0 dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞.
(e) The constant orientation 0 is AEStronglyMeasurable.
(f) Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, so every property holds Hⁿ⌞∅-almost everywhere; in particular `orients` holds.
For every ω we get R₀.action ω = ∫ over ∅ of (…) dHⁿ = 0 = 0·∫ ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) = c·∫ ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y).
2. Case c ≠ 0: the data. Let s := Int.sign c. Since c ≠ 0, s = 1 if c > 0 and s = −1 if c < 0. In both cases s·|c| = c, where |c| = c.natAbs (Int.sign_mul_natAbs). Define R by carrier univ = ℝⁿ, mult y := |c| for all y, and orient y := s·ε for all y; the orientation is a constant n-vector.
3. Case c ≠ 0: fields (a)–(e).
(a) univ is measurable and univ ⊆ univ.
(b) CountablyRectifiable n univ. univ = range(id) for the identity id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Euclid n, which is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id). So Chapter03 countablyRectifiable_range applies.
(c) mult is constant, hence measurable. mult_pos holds because |c| > 0 when c ≠ 0 (Int.natAbs_pos).
(d) For compact K, ∫⁻_{univ∩K} |c| dHⁿ = |c|·Hⁿ(K) = |c|·Lⁿ(K) < ∞ (lintegral_const, Measure.restrict_apply, Hⁿ = Lⁿ, IsCompact.measure_lt_top). So this integral is ≠ ∞.
(e) orient is constant, hence AEStronglyMeasurable.
4. Case c ≠ 0: field (f) `orients`. We prove it at every y, so in particular a.e. Take Q := ⊤, the whole space ℝⁿ.
First, the approximate tangent space. finrank ⊤ = finrank ℝⁿ = n (finrank_top, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and y ∈ ⊤. So Chapter03 hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule with P := ⊤ gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ↑⊤ y ⊤. Since ↑(⊤ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid n)) = univ (Submodule.top_coe), this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n univ y ⊤ for the carrier univ.
Second, the orientation. IsUnitOrientationOf (s·ε) ⊤ holds with τ := e. Indeed, e is orthonormal (OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal). span(range e) = ⊤ because e is a basis (Module.Basis.span_eq applied to (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, whose coercion is e). For every covector α, (s·ε)(α) = s·α(e). This equals α(e) when c > 0 (s = 1, left disjunct) and −α(e) when c < 0 (s = −1, right disjunct).
5. Case c ≠ 0: the action. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ):
R.action ω = ∫_{univ} |c|·(s·ε)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y)
= ∫ |c|·s·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y)   (Measure.restrict_univ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ)
= ∫ c·ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y)   (s·|c| = c)
= c·∫ ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y)   (MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul, which needs no integrability hypothesis).
6. In both cases R is an IMRep in univ with R.action ω = c·∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(y)(e) dLⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ). ∎
Implementation note (not part of the proof): name every auxiliary Lean declaration introduced for this child with the prefix dtc_bc_cz_unit_current_imrep_. Sibling candidates are merged into one Submission.lean, and only byte-identical duplicate declarations are dropped. A direct anonymous-constructor IMRep with the fields above, after a case split on c = 0, suffices.
proof_key_steps: c = 0: the empty triple (∅, 0, 0) is an IMRep (an Hⁿ-null set is countably rectifiable, and every a.e. condition is vacuous). Its action is 0 = c∫ω(e).

c ≠ 0: take (ℝⁿ, |c|, sign(c)·ε) with ε(α) = α(e). ℝⁿ = range(id) is countably rectifiable, and |c| is locally integrable because Hⁿ = Lⁿ is finite on compacts. At every y, ⊤ is an approximate tangent space (hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule), and the orthonormal basis e orients it with sign sign(c).
Action: ∫_{ℝⁿ} |c|·sign(c)·ω(y)(e) dHⁿ = c∫ω(y)(e) dLⁿ, by Hⁿ = Lⁿ, sign(c)|c| = c and integral_const_mul.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple defines a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of U (Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T). Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, R.Represents T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 6.3.1 (‡) (local copy book/chapter-06.txt lines 733–753), where formula (‡) is asserted to define a current. This child is the general form of steps 1–3 of the supplied proof of dtc_bc_cz_unit_current. There, for c ≠ 0, M = ℝⁿ, θ ≡ |c| and ξ ≡ sign(c)·e₁∧…∧eₙ (for c = 0, M = ∅):
- the bound |α(e)| ≤ ‖α‖ of step 1 becomes step 1 below;
- the linearity of step 2 becomes steps 4–5;
- the continuity estimate |Λ(ω_q)| ≤ |c|·Lⁿ(K)·sup_K‖ω_q‖ of step 3 becomes step 6.
This exact frozen type is already comparator-accepted as DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.imrep_current-a1 (Submission.dtc_imrep_current, candidate 642d7450f), and it is reused here unchanged.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. For a covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. Unit orientations have norm at most one. By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then for every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty when n = 0).
2. Measurability. For every continuous n-form ω, the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The reasons: θ is measurable (field measurable_mult; its cast to ℝ is measurable); ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); ω is continuous; and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous because it is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
3. θ is integrable over compact sets. Let K be compact with K ⊆ U. Then 1_K θ is μ-integrable: it is measurable, and its lower integral satisfies ∫⁻ 1_K θ dμ = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict; integrable_indicator_iff). Write C_K := ∫ 1_K θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞) for its (Bochner) integral.
4. Integrability of the integrand. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), let K := tsupport ω (compact and ⊆ U), and let B := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0. By steps 2–3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. Linearity. Define T(ω) := R.action ω for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand for ω + η is the sum of the integrands for ω and η. Both are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) (integral_add). The integrand for cω is c times the integrand for ω, so T(cω) = cT(ω) (integral_const_mul). Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), and R.Represents T holds by definition.
6. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every derivative converges uniformly on K. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖ and D⁰0 = 0), this says ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·C_K (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with step 3). Now let ε > 0 and choose N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/(C_K + 1) for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. Then |T(ω_j)| ≤ εC_K/(C_K + 1) < ε for j ≥ N, so T(ω_j) → 0.
7. By steps 5 and 6, T is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations satisfy |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for a.e. x in M.
For a test form ω, the integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{spt ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ. Hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0, so T is a current.
